The rule these entries are written under -- what a copy is, what the two
markers `[implemented-against: ...]` and `[see: ...]` mean, and why nothing
names a section number or a line range -- lives in ONE place:
`src/SPEC-REFERENCES.md`. It is not restated here; fifteen copies of it had

THE NAMES THIS FILE USES, and the spec each one names:

licensed_by: kogaki#1030 -- this carrier holds the CURRENT control plane only. It is not a version ledger: superseded states, defect specimens and the history of past amendments live in git and in the issues. A change is licensed by an issue, settled by a dated owner decision where it is a decision rather than a transcription, landed here, and recorded by bumping `version` and replacing this line with the issue that licensed it. Ratification is a human act: nothing denies an edit no issue licensed, and these two fields gate no code path.

state_kinds.compute: Runs, writes no owner artifact, does not stop.
state_kinds.write: Runs a renderer bound to it and writes exactly one owner artifact. The renderer is private to the executor (write authority) and renders under the grammar_surface THIS STATE declares, never one bound to the artifact path.
state_kinds.judgment: Reaches a declared judgment point. THE EXECUTOR INVOKES THE JUDGE ITSELF (kogaki#1030): it calls the model named in this table's `judge` block, validates the returned record through this state's own refusals, and retries up to the state's `retries` before failing with the refusal text. The model is a CALLED FUNCTION and never the driver -- the executor still validates and never composes (SPEC-terrain, the typed judgment points).
state_kinds.wait: The executor stops. Nothing further runs until the owner speaks and the session re-enters (SPEC-terrain, the re-entrant executor and the wait rule).
state_kinds.terminal: The run is over. Runs nothing, writes nothing, and the executor stops without awaiting an owner. Distinct from `compute` because a generic interpreter holds no state list of its own (SPEC-terrain, the workflow table) and must read the end from the table rather than from position.

field_semantics.renders_gate_declaration: Required on every state. `true` only where the state declares a gate, and `true` is what SCHEDULES the executor's composition of that state's declaration. It NAMES THE HOOK CHAIN THAT EXECUTES THE GATE and places no obligation on a session: the executor composes the declaration and stops, the harness renders the question the declaration carries, `.claude/hooks/write-gate-capture.py` records the answer at the moment the owner gives it, and that same chain invokes the executor again. It is a statement about the table and never about the runtime asking — the post-tag-selection window's question allowlist is empty and stays empty; the executor writes a file and stops.
field_semantics.conditional: Required on every state. `false` where the state is always entered; otherwise a string naming the condition. Counted by counted_baseline.conditional_states.
field_semantics.writes: Required on every state. `null` where the state writes no owner artifact; otherwise the owner_artifacts key it writes.
field_semantics.grammar_surface: Required on every state whose `writes` is non-null, and absent otherwise. Names the report-format.json surface whose line_class allowlist governs THIS state's render. The binding is per state, never per artifact path (SPEC-terrain, write authority).
field_semantics.gate_id: Required on every state whose `renders_gate_declaration` is true, and absent otherwise. Names the src/gate-registry.json gate the state declares. A property this table exists to carry may not be read off a missing key, so the two conditions are one biconditional over the states array and NOT a count: this note deliberately enumerates no number of gate states, because the count moved from three to four at kogaki#856 and a note carrying it would have gone stale in the same commit — which is the defect kogaki#807 repaired one field over, in the `owner_reads` note that used to read "Three keys" and enumerate them.
field_semantics.retries: Required on every state whose `kind` is `judgment`, and absent otherwise. The number of times the executor RE-ASKS the judge after a response its own refusals rejected; 0 means the first refusal is final. Declared PER STATE rather than once for the table because the states differ in how much a re-ask can plausibly repair -- and declared HERE rather than in the executor because the count is a property of the workflow, which is what this carrier holds.
field_semantics.judge: A table-level block, not a state field. Names the command the executor runs for every judgment state, THE MODEL IT PINS, and the output format it parses. THE MODEL IS PINNED HERE AND NEVER INHERITED FROM THE SESSION (kogaki#1030): a judgment whose model is whatever happened to be driving is not reproducible, and the run record could not say what judged it. `KOGAKI_JUDGE_CLI` overrides the resolved binary FOR FIXTURES ONLY and is how the acceptance fixtures stub the call; it changes no other behaviour and pins no model of its own. It also declares `timeout_s`, the per-CALL bound in seconds -- named apart from the advance hook's own timeout because one bounds a call and the other bounds an advance.

judge.note: The executor invokes this for every `judgment` state: `<command> -p --model <model> --output-format <output_format>`, the state's prompt on stdin, the typed record parsed out of the response. A response the state's refusals reject is re-asked up to that state's `retries` and then the run FAILS with the refusal text -- the judgment provenance state `observed` has a producer from this act on, because the Harness now holds an invocation record its own act wrote. `effort` IS THE PIN'S FOURTH COMPONENT AND IS DECLARED RATHER THAN OBSERVED: the call carries no effort flag, so this names the tier the run declares it is asking at, exactly as the judge pin has always been a declaration. What is no longer a declaration is `model` -- it is now the model the executor actually ran, which is why the pin is worth more after kogaki#1030 than before it, not less. `timeout_s` BOUNDS ONE CALL, and it is derived from the bound around it (PR #1044 round 1): .claude/hooks/advance-terrain.py kills the whole advance at ADVANCE_TIMEOUT_S = 480, and a span can make up to six calls (two judgment states at retries: 2), so a per-call bound above 80s could let one span exhaust the hook and leave the half-finished record that bound exists to relay. 90 is above that ratio deliberately: the arithmetic bounds the WORST case, in which every call is both slow and refused, and pricing the ordinary case at the worst case would make a normal run fail on a slow answer. What the bound guarantees is that a HUNG call cannot consume the advance silently; a span that legitimately needs six slow calls is over the hook budget whatever this value is, and that is the hook timeout relaying a real fact rather than this bound hiding it.

states.ordering: AHEAD OF J3_neighborhood, and that is this row's whole reason for existing at this position (kogaki#861, owner ruling 2026-09-05). The neighborhood judgment names, per candidate, the Thesis candidate it serves; a target can only be refused against a candidate set that already exists, so the ids are FIXED here and J3 reads them. The alternative — one judgment composing candidates and neighborhood together — was declined: the model would supply the list and the targets into it in the same act, and nothing outside that act could refuse a target naming a candidate the same record invented.

owner_surface_coverage.rule: DENOMINATOR = the states in this file whose `writes` is non-null (every surviving owner surface, since write authority makes a writing state the only thing that may write one). NUMERATOR = those of them whose `grammar_surface` names a surface present in report-format.json's `surfaces`. A removed subcommand contributes to NEITHER term: it is not a surviving surface, so removal moves the denominator and never the numerator.
owner_surface_coverage.recomputed_never_transcribed: `at_this_version` is a convenience for a human reader and carries no authority. On any disagreement the rule above wins and the field is repaired — never the rule to the figure. No registered check executes the rule (SPEC what is not carried).

bound_to_a_state.cotags: the cotag_groups state. CALLABLE for composition, REFUSED at the owner artifact: a standalone invocation whose rendering destination resolves to the repository's `reports/` fails rather than writing CoTagGroups.md (write authority). Redirect it and the composition proceeds — a rendering whose lifetime is the run is not an owner artifact (specs/SPEC.md's lifetime discriminator — lifetime, not format or audience-in-principle).
bound_to_a_state.report: the full_report state. Same write authority as `cotags`: callable for composition, and refused where the destination resolves to the repository's `reports/`, so FullReport.md is written only from the writing state the table binds the renderer to (write authority).
bound_to_a_state.run: THE CONTROL PLANE, bound to the table AS A WHOLE rather than to one state: it reads the run record, executes the states this file declares until the next declared WAIT or the TERMINAL, writes that state's artifact, and stops. RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT UNCOVERED (kogaki#901): the totality below is stated over EVERY dispatcher case, and `run` appeared in none of the five maps before this head — a defect against this file by its own rule. It went unseen because nothing computes the totality: no code in this repository reads these maps, so the invariant is prose and its only reader is a person.
bound_to_a_state.start: the same states `run` executes, entered by the harness's SKILL EXPANSION rather than by a hook event (kogaki#1027). It opens the run, advances to its first wait and stops; it refuses an existing run record, so it never resumes one. It is in THIS map and not in `owner_executed_entry_points` for a reason worth stating: the owner types no command here either — the terrain skill file's one `!` line is executed by the harness at invocation, before the model sees anything — so an entry point nobody types belongs with the states it runs. Its transitions carry the `skill-expansion` executor kind and no hook fields, because no hook event produced them.

non_flow_entry_points.self-test: seam-free identity-cite fixture pass; emits no owner surface, carries no sequencing authority
non_flow_entry_points.validate: runs survey-record validation; emits no owner surface

entry_point_accounting: EVERY case in src/terrain.mjs's dispatcher appears in exactly one of the 5 maps above (bound_to_a_state, removed_entry_points, retired_entry_points, non_flow_entry_points, owner_executed_entry_points), and THAT TOTALITY is the property rather than the count: the next entry point is covered by the totality rather than by having been remembered. A case in none of them, or in two, is a defect against this file. THREE MAPS ARE EMPTY AT THIS HEAD AND ALL THREE KEYS STAY. `owner_executed_entry_points` has been empty since v14 (kogaki#856): the owner types no command in this flow. `removed_entry_points` and `retired_entry_points` are emptied at kogaki#901, propagating SPEC-terrain v36 §"A removed entry point is DELETED, and leaves no stub": the nine refusing stubs are gone from the dispatcher, so there is no case left for either map to account for. The keys stay on the same ground the v14 one did — an empty map states the set is empty, where a deleted key would leave a reader unable to tell an empty set from a map somebody dropped. The totality holds over 8 cases and 2 non-empty maps: survey, cotags, compose-input, report, run and start in bound_to_a_state; self-test and validate in non_flow_entry_points. `start` joined at kogaki#1027, and it is the case that made the executor's TWO invocation acts visible in this map rather than one. `default:` is the unknown-command banner and is not a case. THE TOTALITY IS COMPUTED, and by `checks/check-entry-point-accounting.sh` (kogaki#986) — an editor of these maps is told here that a reader exists, because a reader nothing points at is one the next editor works around. Before that member the sentence above was prose whose only reader was a person who happened to look, and at the head before kogaki#901 it did not hold: `run` was a dispatcher case in none of the five maps, and stood across the #856 and #861 sittings, both of which edited these very maps. The sentence STAYS — the check reads it and refuses if it goes, so the declaration and its instrument retire together or not at all.
